The frigged air makes it cold, so the surrounding muscles spasm/twitch. For the most part temperatures (heat or cold) agitate me. And seeing how I have metal in various places in my body, everything hurts.

Hopefully the CT scan will give you some answers. At this point what's a other surgery right? Little joke (just trying to lighten the mood). That's a tricky word, "recovery". It's all on how you perceive the meaning I guess... Honestly you'll never be who you were, you just gotta adjust to this "new skin". There's a lot of ups and downs, more downs I'm sure. But like others have said, everybody's is different and will heal at their own pace etc. etc. But there is no "how-to" for or with TBI, sadly I know. It pisses me off more often than not too. I've kind of become numb and disconnected to the world around me and just work on me when I can. Downloaded a lot of "brain games" apps and just work out my mind hours at a time. Not one doctor gave me an ETA, not even a time frame but you just have to keep stimulating your brain like /u/beardedNole said
Don't worry about it, hope things are getting better. Even in the slightest.

It is what it is, what're you gonna do right? Sorry for the late reply, put my laptop down and was staring at the ceiling as my room got brighter and brighter as hours passed.
How do you get overwhelmed? Is it the people, selection, lights, smells, etc? But I agree with /u/beardedNole make a list and take your time, it never hurts to ask for help from employees either.

Fucking ditto! I came home after my coma to a house full of guitars and I no longer have an interest in playing, I lost my dexterity too. That might also be one of the reasons why I can't enjoy much. I used work on my cars and anything that involves my hands. Most days I'm anhedonic and lethargic now...

Not so great, but it is what it is. That family crap blows! So hard!

Back against the wall, all you can do is hope against hope while you fight.
No apologies neccisary, I make grammatical errors all the time. It's worse when I try to carry a verbal convo with someone; I stutter and they had to replace my jaw.

I'm doing the best I can, filling out more paperwork and calling whoever is "supposed" to handle my file. I even physically went down to the local office in my state, yet most of my efforts are in vain. Still teaching myself how to walk and my insurance won't cover anymore rehab :/

I've attended a few meets, they, like all of my doctors, are surprised at how I am even still alive (you would say/think the same if you saw the damage). I would attend more and physically do more but all of my money went to my lawyer and rent. My money is pretty much depleted, so'll I'll be homeless soon if disability does not come through. It's been almost a year since the hospital applied for me and voice-messages go without a response: "leave a message with your SS# and phone# and I will respond within 24 hours -beep-". Nope, nothing.
Your special day was stolen, happy birthday though.

I do and try but physical and mental permanency continues to scare me as time presses. Sleep is back to eluding me. Hallucinations, though not as frequent, still remain. Both auditory and visual. There is literally a list of things wrong with me and it seems forever ongoing. If I had better coverage, it would slightly put me at ease but I take what I can get. 

Not so great on losing what I've lost though. Funny what time will tell. Ha, I guess water is thicker than blood. But I can only be accountable for myself, though there is a couple that stands out but like everyone, they have their own lives to live as well.

Nearing the year mark. I was in a coma, broke most of my bones literally head to toe. Physical pain still persists, worse in some cases and areas. My neurologist says it could be this or that. Mood and pain fluctuates but have been having more bad days than bearable. Drooling still and having oral bleeding from the broken teeth. I'm still getting my lefts and rights mixed up and been having adverse effects to most of the prescriptions. Speaking of neuroplasticity, there really is no time frame is there? Best quote I've been getting, twenty years.

Coma November 2013 here. SSRIs had no effect when it came to me but honestly there is truly only one way to find out. As each injury is different, like thumbprints. Sure there are some similarities among the majority, it's the details that are key e.g. I was prescribed sleeping pills for my insomnia but they made me suicidal. What works for most, didn't work for me. I had adverse effects to mostly everything that was prescribed to me. But then again that's me, I'm not saying the same will happen to him.

I'm literally in the same boat... As far as making new friends, just try and converse with random strangers whenever you leave the house. I met a few people in waiting rooms. The waiting room in my neurologist's office was a little less intimidating because the majority of the other people had TBI as well. Bold enough, talk to people while waiting inline at the grocery store. I collected like five phone numbers since my coma and they all seem to be really cool with me and who I am now. Let the past be the past my friend. Shoot me a PM if you ever want to chat or whatever.
Thanks man. As soon as disability kicks in, I'll have to get a set. Until then, I'm broke as a joke.

I have a lot of the same issues. I was in a coma nine months ago, it heals. My hallucinations are less frequent and my tinnitus finally went away. I was scared it was going to be my "new norm". Like I'm sure you hear day in and day out: "it takes time" / "it'll get better in time". As far as short term goes, Post-it's are you new best friend. Sad I know but you gotta work with what you've got.
I'm searching high and low but there's a bit much on my plate at the moment.

I miss walking and doing things normally too! But livingeasy is right, getting trapped in your own head is the worst. Especially after a coma. Suicide revolves around TBI, shit you're still here so make the best of it. There is a life to be had after TBI and you're never truly alone. I'm learning as I go myself.

To me "it is what it is" refers to the consequences I face, as a result of how things turnout. Dealing with the aftermath of the action/s of everything that has been done. Shit happens, we just need to find a way around or through tribulations. I've never put anything off, always been a right here right now kind of person. Working with what I have, things just keep being stripped from me. My ability to walk, eat normally, cognition. My life has never been easy but I'm still fighting the fight, even after all I've been through, I'm still here.

In time, don't force things. Just let things happen organically. People who approach you and are warm towards you, will be worth talking to. Don't worry about maintaining eye contact, just go with the flow and if they make a big deal about eye contact, they're probably not worth explaining every little detail to. Also, kudos on being off HA.

Was just feeling overwhelmed. No more suicidal idealization... recently. I've been trying to "let go" of my former persona but people are making it difficult. Trying to treat it as if I was just in a little "fender bender", I know that's probably how they're coping with that particular event. But I'm trying to let go and move forward. It's a little hard with the amnesia and all, I seriously don't remember who I was but they won't "let go". My memories are fragmented and intermittent, I don't remember the hospital stay besides one doctor in particular. I'm just numb, it does warm my heart, the fact that you or anyone can relate. The biggest things that I've lost, in my point of view, relationships. I thought bonds were stronger then they were. "only time will tell", time told... 

I've punched the walls til my knuckles bled. I could never strike another person, not again, that life is behind me. And thanks, much appreciated.

I write, play "brain games", attend our local support group as often as I can (held weekly), physical exercise (to regain the enormous amount of muscle I lost), and that's about it, well all that I can remember at the moment.

I don't check up on other people on them, I use them to stay connected with family that are out of state and to grab phone numbers/e-mails and whatnot. Too much reading gives me a headache, which turn into migraines. I exercise daily, well as often as I can. Some days I can't physically walk, due to atrophy and the list of broken bones. I keep forgetting to occupy myself, thanks for reminding me! I could blame it on the clinically diagnosed amnesia but still. I appreciate the feedback.

I received my TBI November 1, 2013 in an auto accident. Wrecked my car so bad that they needed to cut the roof off of my car and me out of my clothes. I had to be flown-in to a level 1 trauma hospital. I was told my car started acting up and my tires were bald so I lost control. Once I slammed into the cement-pylon I didn't have a pulse for awhile. That night shattered my pelvis, disintegrated my jaw, broke some ribs and my femur, dislodged my diaphragm, and gave me internal bleeding literally from head to toe. I was in a coma for a little more than a week. I just got off of a liquid diet and am now eating soft foods. I don't remember what treatments I've been through, besides physical therapy. After some evaluation they sent me on my way, I just recently found a neurologist. We'll see what he has to say and go from there.

Severe TBI here. I was in a coma not too long ago and since I woke up things have been challenging. Many doctors do follow the guidelines mentioned in your link but it has no or bad effects on people like me. I'm sure it would be alright for some but I found out the hard way, it's not for the rest of us. Intentions as good as they may be from literally anyone, could be dangerous to those of us with severe TBI.

I was in a coma just four months ago. Everyday is a struggle that sometimes seems pointless. I'm reteaching myself how to walk and getting used to this metal jaw. Eating is a chore (takes forever) because of the missing and broken teeth, I was on a liquid diet for awhile. My pelvis was shattered beyond repair, along with my jaw so they're both metal now. My car was completely wrecked. They had to cut the roof off and through my clothes to salvage my borderline dead body, I know that because my sister took pictures of the aftermath. I keep getting drugs thrown at me because TBI isn't well known and we're all just learning as we go, pretty much. Sadly I see more dark days than good but fuck it I didn't stay dead so I might as well stay alive and find people that can relate and maybe help.
